Using the county tables

  • Each state section ends with its counties' share of the statewide vote and what each candidate gets there at any statewide result: move the slider, or use the buttons for a tie, a 3-point win either way or the model's margin.
  • When a county has finished counting, type its two main candidates' percentages. The table turns them into the statewide margin they imply, and the box above it combines every county you've entered, weighted by size.
  • Each row shows the county's voting bloc, a group of counties with similar demographics in the Census Bureau's latest estimates (rules at the start of section 4). Pick a bloc to list all its counties and see its combined line.
  • Partial counts mislead: early and mail votes usually come first and Election Day votes later. In Georgia, Texas and Iowa you can mark an entry as early/mail only to compare it with that county's early-vote benchmark instead.
  • Method: uniform swing on the log-odds scale from recent results (each table says which). In past races counties landed a typical 1-5 points from their line, and one big county alone has misread the state by up to 10 points (section 5). Candidates' home areas aren't modeled. Your entries stay in this browser only.
